QNznD9hMEh0.title: Jim Simons (full length interview) - Numberphile
QNznD9hMEh0.summary: The full-length Numberphile interview with mathematician and hedge fund founder Jim Simons. He discusses his path from mathematics and codebreaking to founding Renaissance Technologies, his use of algorithms in markets, and his philanthropy.
QNznD9hMEh0.why: HN recommends it as the best readily available interview with Simons, notable for his emphasis on luck and a humble approach to success.

quote.text: the full length one is very good. it gives an understanding as to why simons has been so successful.

Sm5xF-UYgdg.title: How not to be ignorant about the world | Hans and Ola Rosling
Sm5xF-UYgdg.summary: Hans Rosling and his son Ola run an audience quiz with global population, health and income data to show how wrong most people are about the world. Ola then gives four ways to get less ignorant.
Sm5xF-UYgdg.why: Recommended as evidence that the world is improving despite negative news, and for how people misjudge global trends.

quote.text: I promise it is not a waste of your time.

ynbgMKclWWc.title: Democracy at Work: Curing Capitalism | Richard Wolff | Talks at Google
ynbgMKclWWc.summary: Economist Richard Wolff's Talks at Google lecture on his book Democracy at Work. He critiques capitalism and argues for worker-run cooperatives as a path to a more democratic economy.
ynbgMKclWWc.why: HN commenters share it as an accessible case for worker cooperatives and workplace democracy as a model for a modern left.

quote.text: I recently came across an interesting talk by Richard Wolff at Google [1]

4d0EGIt1SPc.title: The REAL Possibility of Mapping Alien Planets!
4d0EGIt1SPc.summary: PBS Space Time explains the proposal to use the Sun's gravity as a giant lens, sending a train of small light-sail spacecraft to the focal point roughly 550 AU out. It covers how such a telescope could image exoplanets in surprising detail and the engineering challenges involved.
4d0EGIt1SPc.why: It is the go-to explanation whenever a thread touches on imaging exoplanets or solar gravitational lens telescopes.

quote.text: Pretty good explanation of the technique and challenges involved

GoW8Tf7hTGA.title: Star Size Comparison 2
GoW8Tf7hTGA.summary: A visual scale comparison of stars and cosmic objects, from planets up to some of the largest known stars, set to music. It is meant to convey the vastness of the universe.
GoW8Tf7hTGA.why: Shared as a go-to humbling look at cosmic scale, noted for its chilling audio and visuals pairing.

quote.text: The combination of audio and content of this video gives me chills.

9F9ahZQ7oP0.title: RetroAhoy: The Secret of Monkey Island
9F9ahZQ7oP0.summary: A roughly 75-minute video essay from Ahoy's RetroAhoy series on the making and history of The Secret of Monkey Island. It covers the small LucasArts team, the game's development and its sequel.
9F9ahZQ7oP0.why: Recommended as a well-made documentary-style history that gives context around the game and inspires replays.

quote.text: Do yourself a favor and watch this wonderful video essay historique on The Monkey Island series from Ahoy

gwvA49ZXnf8.title: Call Between Alexey Navalny and FSB Officer Konstantin Kudryavtsev [English Subtitles]
gwvA49ZXnf8.summary: Bellingcat's publication of the recorded call in which Alexey Navalny, posing as a security aide, gets FSB officer Konstantin Kudryavtsev to describe the operation to poison him. It has English subtitles.
gwvA49ZXnf8.why: HN cites it as a striking confession obtained through caller ID spoofing and social engineering.

quote.text: But the best part is how he did it: caller ID spoof + social engineering.

8JrqH2oOTK4.title: Turning Smashed TVs into Realistic Artificial Daylight
8JrqH2oOTK4.summary: DIY Perks shows how to turn old or smashed TVs and monitors into realistic artificial window lights, using the backlight and Fresnel lens to simulate distant daylight.
8JrqH2oOTK4.why: HN points to it in threads on artificial sunlight, as a buildable and surprisingly convincing artificial window.

quote.text: The result is quite stunning. I've never seen anything like it.

BiqDZlAZygU.title: In full: Rowan Atkinson on free speech
BiqDZlAZygU.summary: Rowan Atkinson's speech at the launch of the Reform Section 5 campaign in Parliament in 2012. He argues against criminalizing insulting words and for answering speech with more speech.
BiqDZlAZygU.why: Recommended as an eloquent defense of free speech against laws on offensive or insulting speech.

quote.text: Rowan Atkinson made an excellent speech on the matter back then [2]

c2lgEyNaop4.title: Classic Game Postmortem: Alone in the Dark
c2lgEyNaop4.summary: Frederick Raynal gives a GDC postmortem of Alone in the Dark, the game that helped create the survival horror genre. He covers how the team built it and shows some of the old tools used.
c2lgEyNaop4.why: HN commenters recommend it as a firsthand account from the creator, including the old tooling.

quote.text: There is a very nice presentation [1] in which Raynal shows some of the old tools that were used to create Alone in the Dark.

ncPyMUfNyVM.title: Andreas Antonopoulos - 51% Bitcoin Attack
ncPyMUfNyVM.summary: A two-minute clip of Andreas Antonopoulos explaining why a 51% attack on Bitcoin would not destroy it and what such an attack would cost. It is a succinct take on mining security.
ncPyMUfNyVM.why: HN commenters link it as a short, favorite explanation of Bitcoin's security and the sustainability of a 51% attack.

quote.text: Andreas Antonopoulos has a good take on this for Bitcoin

F-yDKeya4SU.title: America Was Wrong About Ethanol - Study Shows
F-yDKeya4SU.summary: Engineering Explained examines new research suggesting corn ethanol in US gasoline may emit as much or more carbon than gasoline. It covers the Renewable Fuel Standard and why ethanol was assumed to be a green fuel.
F-yDKeya4SU.why: Cited as an accessible summary of evidence that corn ethanol is no better than gasoline for emissions.

quote.text: Corn-based ethanol is at best as bad a carbon emitter as gasoline, and it's most likely worse.

dGiQaabX3_o.title: What Happened Before History? Human Origins
dGiQaabX3_o.summary: Kurzgesagt's animated overview of human origins and the vast prehistory before recorded history. It covers how modern humans emerged and spread.
dGiQaabX3_o.why: HN commenters recommend it as a compact, well-sourced intro to human evolution that even led one viewer to read Sapiens.

quote.text: there is a great 10 minute video from the Youtube Kurzgesagt channel that lead me to read Sapiens.

nQHBAdShgYI.title: Why Teleportation Would Kill You
nQHBAdShgYI.summary: CGP Grey asks whether Star Trek-style teleportation would kill you and recreate a copy, working through the philosophy of identity and the Ship of Theseus. It is a short animated explainer.
nQHBAdShgYI.why: Pointed to in threads about mind uploading and teleportation as a good, accessible look at personal identity.

quote.text: CGP Grey has a good look at the question wrt Star Trek teleportation

4lmW2tZP2kU.title: Office Space - If I had a million dollars
4lmW2tZP2kU.summary: A 54-second clip from the film Office Space in which two coworkers talk about what they would do with a million dollars. The answers contrast blue-collar and white-collar attitudes toward work.
4lmW2tZP2kU.why: Mostly a joke reference in threads about layoffs, idleness and wealth, with one commenter sincerely recommending the clip for its contrast of work attitudes.

quote.text: Highly recommend to watch the clip from the movie Office Space (only 54 sec long)

D7GDTZ45TRw.title: The Mill CPU Architecture – The Compiler (10 of 13)
D7GDTZ45TRw.summary: A long Mill Computing lecture on the Mill CPU's compiler toolchain, covering the specializer that targets family members, scheduling and latency passes, and the belt. It explains how the compiler handles a wide-issue, exposed-pipeline design.
D7GDTZ45TRw.why: Cited as the authoritative source on how Mill's VLIW-style compiler specializes code and differs from Itanium.

quote.text: have a design talk that covers these concepts wonderfully in the general form

i3D7XYQExt0.title: Calculating a Car Crash - Numberphile
i3D7XYQExt0.summary: Numberphile's Ben Sparks works through the physics of a car crash, showing how kinetic energy grows with the square of speed and why stopping distance climbs so quickly as velocity increases.
i3D7XYQExt0.why: Used as a short explainer when people need to illustrate why speed matters so much in braking and crash severity.

quote.text: There's also a great video I stumbled across yesterday

juWaO5TJS00.title: Lego-style apartment transforms into infinite spaces
juWaO5TJS00.summary: A tour of Christian Schallert's 24 square meter apartment in Barcelona, designed so that it looks like an empty cube until he builds the furniture he needs. Kirsten Dirksen shows how the space is transformed for cooking, sleeping and dressing.
juWaO5TJS00.why: HN people link it as an example of a transformable small apartment in threads on micro-apartments and space-saving furniture.

quote.text: I like this guy's sliding lego house

7xH7eGFuSYI.title: Adam Ruins Everything - Why You Should Tell Coworkers Your Salary
7xH7eGFuSYI.summary: A four-minute Adam Ruins Everything segment on why employers discourage workers from sharing salaries. It argues that discussing pay with coworkers is legal and helps workers.
7xH7eGFuSYI.why: Linked in threads on pay and compensation as a quick explanation of why talking about salary helps employees.

ptUj8JRAYu8.title: Markus Kayser - Solar Sinter Project
ptUj8JRAYu8.summary: Markus Kayser's Solar Sinter project video shows a machine in the desert using sunlight and sand to 3D print glass objects. It is a short demonstration of desert manufacturing from renewable energy and local material.
ptUj8JRAYu8.why: HN references it as prior art whenever solar sintering, sand printing or sunlight-based manufacturing comes up.
